analyst_view.overall: Fulham are 15th under Alvaro Arbeloa, unbeaten in five league games but low-scoring; Emile Smith Rowe is a doubt with a hip problem that Arbeloa does not think is serious, Tom Cairney is fit again and reserve keeper Lecomte is out. Bournemouth are 5th on a club-record nine straight wins under Marco Rose and play Celta Vigo away in the Europa League on Thursday (17:45 UK), three days before this. Rose says there are no new injuries, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi are back, and he rotates because of the schedule; Juanlu Sanchez, Toth and Araujo are out or doubtful. The numbers already count Fulham's heavy card count lately and Stuart Attwell's high card rate.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals: 1.2 for Fulham and 1.3 for Bournemouth, already counting Bournemouth conceding only twice in six. The Thursday trip to Vigo could cost Bournemouth some freshness, but Rose rotates and has Scott and Kroupi back for depth, so that points both ways and I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.7 corners, fairly even, with Fulham's high corner count lately already counted. Both teams play wide and cross a lot, and nothing in the news changes that, so I stay at about 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.0 cards, which is already high: they count Fulham being booked far more than usual lately (+20%) and Stuart Attwell's high rate (+17%). Bournemouth are booked less, and it is not a derby, so I stay at about 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 26.0 shots, 13.5 for Fulham and 12.5 for Bournemouth. Bournemouth play in Vigo on Thursday evening and fly back with about three days to recover, which the numbers do not count, while Fulham have a free week, so I take about 3% off, to about 25.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 8.3 shots on target, already lowered because Bournemouth allow very few and Fulham have been less accurate lately. Bournemouth's travel might cost a little sharpness, but Rose's rotation should protect key attackers, so I stay at about 8.3.
